transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-14
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE); Diego Marquez (Redwood SE); Priya Shah (Helios SRE); Liam O'Connor (Helios Platform PM); Nina Rao (Helios Security)

Summary:
Quick handoff after last week's production incident (token burst + KV cache thrash). Discussed proposed mitigations, temporary runbook changes, and regulatory artifacts needed for Helios audit. Agreed on immediate fallbacks and a controlled load test. Action items assigned.

Topics:
- Incident recap and immediate mitigation review
- Short-term failover and canary plan for dedicated pool
- KV cache warmup and prefix caching strategy
- Compliance artifacts (SOC 2, KMS, data residency) and audit timeline
- Next steps: RCA draft, load test, pricing/credits

Action items (quick):
- Diego: KV cache warmup script and test plan
- Jamie: pricing/credits and dedicated burst config
- Priya: share logs and traces
- Nina: compliance checklist items

Transcript:
[15:00] Jamie Park: Hey everyone, thanks for making time on short notice. I know last week was rough so—uh—wanted to do a quick recovery handoff and make sure we're aligned on mitigations and audit asks.
[15:12] Priya Shah: Yeah thanks. We had a bunch of 500s during the spike and then saw the KV cache evaporate, so we had a high tail latency for a while, and then the fallback to the smaller model was... kinda slow.
[15:25] Diego Marquez: Right. From our side we traced the initial failure mode to a mix of continuous batching + large seq lengths causing memory pressure on one of the dedicated nodes. The KV cache eviction policy then kicked in and warmed very slowly.
[15:40] Liam O'Connor: Quick clarifying q: when you say "dedicated nodes" you mean the dedicated pool we spun up three weeks ago, not hosted, right?
[15:46] Diego Marquez: Correct, the Dedicated pool. It was under a mixed workload (some long context chat sessions, some embeddings) which increased variance.
[15:55] Nina Rao: From security side, auditors asked about KMS/HSM integration and audit logs for the fallback window. We need the artifacts sooner rather than later.
[16:05] Jamie Park: Yep, we'll attach SOC 2 doc and a KMS integration guide. I'll share links. Diego, can you also confirm whether key material ever touched customer nodes or remained in Redwood-managed HSM?
[16:17] Diego Marquez: To my knowledge keys were in Redwood-managed KMS for that environment, no customer key export. I'll double-check and provide an explicit statement.
[16:27] Priya Shah: There were also some edge cases where the router sent traffic to a node that still had a memory leak from an old model version—maybe the rollout didn't fully complete. That was visible in the traces I sent yesterday but the timestamps are a bit messy.
[16:40] Diego Marquez: Hmm, rollout incomplete—yeah that could cause the mismatch. We saw two versions active for a short window. Our rollout system tries to avoid split-brain but under heavy load it can be delayed.
[16:52] Liam O'Connor: So the ask from Helios is: 1) a short-term runbook we can use if this happens again, 2) an assurance for auditors, and 3) a plan for a controlled load test to prove the fix.
[17:03] Jamie Park: Sounds right. For short-term we recommend: enable prefix/KV cache warmup for the heavy routes, lower the canary threshold so rollouts wait for warm cache, and provision burst capacity for 2 hours during your peak.
[17:15] Priya Shah: On the warmup—do you have a script for that? Right now we had to manually replay requests which is painful.
[17:24] Diego Marquez: We do. I'll produce a KV cache warmup script and a test plan. It will do sequential preloads by user prefix and validate TTLs. We'll include failure modes and auto-retry.
[17:35] Nina Rao: Great. Also auditors want a timeline that shows when fallbacks occurred and whether any PII was logged during that window. We need a statement about data retention and whether logs include full request payloads.
[17:47] Diego Marquez: Logs are redacted by default; we only store request metadata for X days. But I'll create a short doc that outlines log retention, redaction policy, and the specific artifacts we can provide for the audit.
[17:58] Priya Shah: One more infra note: during the spike our router ephemeral queue length exceeded the configured burst and started shedding. Is there a way to configure a soft limit to buffer for a few seconds instead of immediate shed?
[18:10] Jamie Park: There's a couple levers. We can increase the queue size on the router or add a small elastic buffer layer. But both impact latency/cost. For immediate mitigation, we suggested fallback to a smaller model variant which lowers memory and latency. But you mentioned that fallback felt slow—what was the rolloff time?
[18:26] Priya Shah: About 45–60 seconds to stabilize because the cache warmup was sequential and the first requests still hit cold paths.
[18:34] Diego Marquez: If we do aggressive prefix warmup + a short-lived in-memory cache snapshot for the new node, we can bring that down to under 10 seconds in many cases. The tradeoff is a short spike in GPU memory upfront.
[18:45] Liam O'Connor: Okay. What's the test plan look like? We want reproducibility and clear pass/fail criteria so our platform team can sign off.
[18:54] Diego Marquez: Test plan: 1) create a controlled replica of the workflow on a dedicated pool; 2) run ramp tests that include long-context sessions and embeddings mixes; 3) introduce a simulated node failure; 4) measure tail latency percentiles and time-to-stabilize. Pass criteria: p99 under X ms and stabilization under 15s. I'll put exact numbers in the doc.
[19:10] Jamie Park: For the audit artifacts, Nina, we'll share our SOC 2 summary, KMS integration notes, and a short statement about where keys are held. I'll include a link to the console section showing token-level LC.
[19:20] Nina Rao: Please also include the API access logs that show which service accounts performed the fallback—it's important for chain-of-custody in our compliance pipeline.
[19:28] Diego Marquez: We can provide a CSV extract of service-account events for that window.
[19:33] Priya Shah: One operational request: can Redwood enable a temporary escalation channel? Like an on-call bridge we can hit if we see this again tonight.
[19:41] Jamie Park: Yes we can open a P1 bridge for the next 48 hours. I'll set that up and send details.
[19:47] Liam O'Connor: Appreciate it. Also regarding pricing—we need to know the incremental cost for keeping burst capacity reserved for the week after the audit.
[19:55] Jamie Park: I'll send a temporary credits offer and a pricing delta for dedicated burst in the follow-up email.
[20:02] Diego Marquez: One minor nit—during the incident we saw the router report a "k-v cash" error in the transcript logs; some of the terms were mangled in the auto transcriber. The actual metric is kv_cache_hit_ratio dropping below 0.2.
[20:17] Priya Shah: Haha yeah the transcriber always changes things, but the metric is what we care about.
[20:21] Jamie Park: OK to recap: Diego will produce KV cache warmup script and the controlled load test plan; Jamie will send RCA draft, pricing/temporary credits, and enable the 48-hour bridge; Priya will provide traces and sample request IDs; Nina will confirm the compliance checklist items; we'll regroup after the load test and after the RCA draft is shared.
[20:38] Priya Shah: Sounds good. Can we get the RCA by Thursday?
[20:42] Jamie Park: Yes, draft by 2026-09-17 EOD. Finalized after your feedback.
[20:46] Liam O'Connor: Can we schedule the load test for the following Tuesday? Gives us time to prep.
[20:50] Diego Marquez: Tuesday works, I'll coordinate with your infra on exact timing.
[20:53] Nina Rao: Thanks all.
[20:54] Jamie Park: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with notes and the doc links.

End of meeting.
